item.title: China’s Teapots May Boost Iran Oil Buying as Stockpiles Dwindle
item.description: Shrinking regional oil stockpiles held by China’s independent refiners in Shandong province may spur increased buying of Iranian crude, offering Tehran a needed boost after a period of slow sales.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Gold Climbs Above $4,400 as Traders Turn Focus to US Inflation
item.description: Gold advanced to a two-month high above $4,400 an ounce ahead of a key US inflation report that could provide fresh clues to the Federal Reserve’s appetite for an interest-rate hike.
item.dc:creator: Robin Paxton

item.title: Oil Holds Advance, Yen in Focus After Weakening: Markets Wrap
item.description: Oil kept its gains from a four-day rally as fading hopes for a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz revived inflation concerns before key US data later this week. Asian stocks were little changed.
item.dc:creator: Anand Krishnamoorthy

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 11
item.description: Oil held a four-day gain after US President Donald Trump made sweeping new demands on Iran, clouding the outlook for a deal to reopen the crucial Strait of Hormuz.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Tencent’s WorkBuddy Sparks AI Turnaround Hopes After Stock Rout
item.description: Tencent Holdings Ltd.’s early success with WorkBuddy may give the Chinese Internet giant a chance to catch up after lagging peers in the artificial intelligence race for the past few years.
item.dc:creator: Jeanny Yu

item.title: Colombia Inflation Unexpectedly Slows, Easing Pressure on Rates
item.description: Colombia’s inflation rate cooled last month, offering some relief to the central bank after policymakers recently surprised investors by keeping borrowing costs unchanged.
item.dc:creator: Oscar Medina

item.title: Traders Are Piling Into Taiwan Dollar Options to Bet on Rebound
item.description: Currency traders are stepping up bullish options bets on the Taiwan dollar, signaling a shift in sentiment after the currency suffered its worst July since 2015.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: SEC Alleges Fund Adviser Misled Investors in Pre-IPO Schemes
item.description: Investment adviser Adit Ventures and co-founder Eric Munson were accused by the US Securities and Exchange Commission of making false claims about investments and overcharging clients with millions of dollars in undisclosed fees to buy shares of companies including SpaceX and Klarna before they were offered to the public.
item.dc:creator: Nicola M White

item.title: ETFs Look Safer After Bitcoin Hack, Small Caps | ETF IQ 8/10/2026
item.description: "Bloomberg ETF IQ" focuses on the opportunities, risks and current trends tied to the trillions of dollars in the global exchange traded funds industry. Today's guests: JPMorgan Investment Management Chief ETF Strategist Jon Maier, BlackRock Head of Digital Assets Robert Mitchnick, Avantis Investors CIO Eduardo Repetto, and Raymond James Vice President of ETF Strategy Mayuranki De. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 777 Partners Files Bankruptcy After Creditors’ Liquidation Push
item.description: Alternative investment firm 777 Partners has filed for bankruptcy weeks after creditors sought to liquidate what’s left of the company that began unloading its assets more than a year ago.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Randles

item.title: Outsiders Pay $6,500 for Help With Sorority Rush
item.description: The push by young women to gain acceptance into sororities at large schools in the Deep South has led to an increase in demand for rush coaches. Bloomberg News Reporter Gabriel Baumgaertner discusses his recent story about the high price tag some parents are willing to invest to help their kids get into the sorority of their dreams. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Touts $3B in Mineral Project to Counter China
item.description: During a recent meeting with top industry executives, the US President announced $3 billion in investments aimed at strengthening the domestic critical minerals and mining sector. The initiative seeks to reduce reliance on supply chains dominated by China. Gary Evans, Chairman and CEO of US Antimony, participated in the discussion and spoke to Bloomberg News about how much he is willing to see the government invest in his firm. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hims & Hers Lowers Profit Forecast, Shares Drop
item.description: Hims & Hers Health shares are down after the telehealth firm reduced the top end of its adjusted Ebitda forecast for the full year. Madison Muller reports on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Chicago Taps Fitch Senior Director as New CFO Amid Rash of Exits
item.description: Chicago is hiring Ashlee Gabrysch, a senior director at Fitch Ratings, as its next chief financial officer, according to a person familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Shruti Date Singh

item.title: Yen Erases Half of Intervention Gains as Traders Test Bessent
item.description: The yen has wiped out half of its rally from recent interventions by Japan and the US to boost the currency, a psychologically significant move for traders who remain on alert for further official support.
item.dc:creator: Anya Andrianova and John Cheng

item.title: Gautam Adani Wins Dismissal of US Securities Fraud Charges
item.description: Gautam Adani won dismissal of US securities fraud charges, ending a blockbuster case that threatened the expansion of the Indian billionaire’s giant conglomerate.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Hurtado and David Voreacos

item.title: JBS Returns Leadership to Batista Clan as Scion Named CEO
item.description: The world’s largest meat supplier, JBS NV, will be led once again by a member of Brazil’s Batista family, a pivotal move for a global food powerhouse that’s increasingly focused on the US.
item.dc:creator: Dayanne Sousa

item.title: AI Stock Heavy ETF Risks Spread to Broader Equity Market
item.description: A growing share of equity leverage is riding on the same AI names, many of which have seen historic swings.
item.dc:creator: Jin Wu, Denitsa Tsekova and Denise Lu

item.title: Gold Nears $4,400 as Traders Weigh Hormuz Standoff, Inflation
item.description: Gold rose to nearly $4,400 an ounce as traders assessed the latest development around the Strait of Hormuz while awaiting the release of a key US inflation report later this week.
item.dc:creator: Yvonne Yue Li

item.title: Gotham Greens CEO: Not Good To Have an Outbreak Like This
item.description: Craig Stevenson, CEO of Gotham Greens, addressed the ongoing concerns over food safety amid recent recalls linked to salmonella in jalapenos and the widespread Cyclospora outbreak affecting thousands in the U.S. He noted a temporary decline in consumer demand for greens as news of outbreaks circulates, but emphasized that consumer interest in salads remains strong. He speaks with David Gura & Isabelle Lee on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)
